pr_title: [apm-data] Apply lazy rollover on index template creation
pr_body:
Trigger a lazy rollover of existing data streams regardless of whether the index template is being created or updated. This ensures that the apm-data plugin will roll over data streams that were previously using the Fleet integration package.

Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/116230

issue_context.title: apm-data plugin does not automatically roll over existing APM data streams when upgrading to 8.15.x
issue_context.body:
### Elasticsearch Version

8.15.0

### Installed Plugins

_No response_

### Java Version

_bundled_

### OS Version

N/A

### Problem Description

The apm-data plugin installs index templates that should trigger a lazy rollover for data streams with matching index patterns, if the index templates have the highest priority. The rollover logic is only triggering on upgrade, and not on the first installation, so data streams that were previously managed by the Fleet integration package will not be rolled over automatically when upgrading.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an 8.14.x Elastic Cloud deployment, send some APM data to populate data streams
2. Upgrade deployment to 8.15.x
3. Observe that none of the data streams have been (lazily) rolled over

### Logs (if relevant)

_No response_

review_comments: IIUC, for other plugins (like otel-data plugin) that are using IndexTemplateRegistry this would be a no-op since there would be no datastreams to apply rollover too -- Is this correct? Maybe we should have a test to assert this behavior as a follow-up i.e. check if `rollover_on_write` flag is `false` for a datastream created after the plugin is installed?

I'm not sure I understand the scenario. Do you mean a negative check, verifying something that does not match the index pattern is rolled over? I think the existing `IndexTemplateRegistryTests.testAutomaticRollover` covers that: it creates two logs and one traces data stream, and verifies that only the logs ones are rolled over when updating the logs template.

Not exactly a negative check -- my concern is when plugins operate under normal circumstances then there is no need to rollover on installation. I was thinking of having a test case to cover this scenario to make sure that rollover on installation doesn't break anything for other plugins. Does it make sense?
